text:
Sam: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a smaller RBAC surface for services + a lightweight service actor model. want to capture tradeoffs before i write the PR.
Nisha: +1 to narrowing surface. main worry is cross-project service-to-service calls and least-privilege enforcement.
Jamie: curious — do you mean permanent API keys for services or short-lived tokens minted by a service identity?
Sam: thinking short-lived tokens issued by authn service, but with optional long-lived API keys for infra-only integrations. rule: long-lived keys should be scoped and audited heavily.
Alex: can we avoid adding a new token protocol? we already have service accounts + KMS. maybe extend that actor record with `roles` + `allowed_projects`.
Nisha: extending actor record is fine, but we need two axes: org/project scope and call-origin (human vs service). different policies for each.
Sam: agreed. sketching modes: `human-user` tokens (OIDC), `service-ephemeral` (1-60m), `service-static` (rotate every 90d). also need machine-to-machine delegation (impersonation).
Jamie: tradeoff: ephemeral tokens are great for security but add complexity to rollout and retries. if token refresh fails, you must fallback gracefully.
Sam: right — propose built-in fallback policy: ephemeral token failures -> attempt `service-static` if allowed, then reject. fallback configured per-actor.
Alex: how about format for scoping? e.g. `scope: projects:prod:read, projects:staging:write, org:billing:admin` — simple list of ACL tuples.
Nisha: prefer explicit binding to resources rather than freeform strings. e.g. `bindings: [ { role: "read", resource: "project/prod" } ]`. easier for policy engine.
Sam: yep, that matches the policy engine idea. also want a high-level `role` abstraction for UX (dev, infra, ops) that maps to bindings under the hood.
Jamie: what about service discovery and service-account leak syndrome? If many services get long-lived keys, blast radius grows. ops should be able to zone credentials by network/vpc and project.
Nisha: add `credential_zones` — restrict where static keys can be used (cidr / vpc tags). plus revocation lists and emergency rotate APIs.
Alex: implementation note: runtime routing needs a cheap check for allowed_projects to decide caching/kv sharding. don't want to call the policy engine on every token validation. add a token introspection cache keyed by token id + small ttl.
Sam: good. caching TTL policy: ephemeral tokens short TTL equal to token expiry; static tokens use 5m cache with eviction on revocation.
infra-bot: buildkite: job 3821 passed — token-introspect-cache PoC merged to staging: https://ci.example/builds/3821 :shipit:
Jamie: ok for v1: enforce these invariants — (1) all service actors must have explicit `allowed_projects`, (2) service static keys are opt-in and require two approvals, (3) ephemeral tokens are default for new service actors.
Nisha: +1. we should also record `actor.origin` for audit: e.g. `origin: k8s/serviceAccount/x` or `origin: dedicated-runner`. helps debug impersonation.
Sam: will draft a short RFC with these sections: model, token types, scoping schemas, policy/engine integration, runtime caching, migration plan (rotate off static keys), and operational playbooks.
Jamie: can you add a migration checklist for customers using `legacy-service-key`? need a compatibility plan.
Sam: yep — will include a migration mode: `compat -> warn -> enforce` with metrics.
Alex: small nit: ensure telemetry tags include `actor_id`, `project_id`, `token_type` to help SLO/rate-limiting alignment.
Nisha: awesome. Sam — ping when draft is up, will review for compliance wording (audit logs, KMS integration).
Sam: will post draft PR tomorrow. thanks all :raised_hands:
